value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for renaming products, repositories and pages and rewriting every reference to the new names
value.lets_workers: Turn a rename decision into a map, inventory every spelling of every old name across exact commits, plan and make the rewrites in local copies, check every link without relying on redirects, have the owner record the renames only they can do on hosts, sweep until no old name remains outside an allowed context, and draft a plain notice for each retired address.

flow.when: As soon as a rename map is decided.
From the inventory; the owner's host acts are listed separately.
Per repository, in a local copy.
When the owner has renamed repositories, sites or addresses on their hosts.
After rewrites and host renames, and again before calling the rename done.
Last; it decides clean or not.
For each retired address that will keep showing something.

guardrails: No redirect is relied on: every link points at the new address directly.
Old names stay only in named allowed contexts such as provenance and history.
Renaming on hosts is the owner's act; workers edit local copies and check.

value.title: How a rename reaches every reference
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: A person decides the rename map: old and new names, addresses and where old names may stay.
build-inventory finds every variant of every old name at exact commits.
plan-rewrites groups edits per file and lists what only a person can change.
rewrite-references edits local copies and runs each repository's own checks.
The owner renames repositories, sites and addresses on their hosts and records it with record-host-renames.
check-links resolves every link and records redirects and failures.
sweep-old-names decides clean or not; write-archive-notice drafts what old addresses say.
rules: Status lines, commit messages for new work, captions and alt text count; history and receipts do not change.
A redirect that happens to work is still a violation of a clean rename.
Text inside images and videos goes to a person; workers list it, never guess it.
A name that keeps coming back is a finding with a guard, not another sweep.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.
